a4-b158-b155:
Most sober people don't feel much from zeolite, but its effect becomes more obvious when the trip is toxic or the gut is driving it. I put a spoonful of zeolite into a cup of water or juice and sip slowly (some people need a teaspoon, others a tablespoon). Rubbing the zeolite on the body or simply holding the jar also helps me.

In my experiments, zeolite has to be prepared correctly. I use powdered zeolite rather than nano-liquid zeolite. Many products did nothing for me, I think because most zeolites have clogged pores that haven't been cleaned, but ZeoCharge is sold as cleaned.
a4-b156-b157:
For my ozonated zeolite, I mix the powder into water and use an ozone-water purifier in a glass vessel because ozone destroys plastic. I mean ozonating water, never inhaling ozone gas. With a machine producing about two grams of ozone per hour, ten minutes produced a working zeolite for me, however much zeolite was in the water. Less time did not work as well, and more time did not noticeably improve it.

Zeolite binds metals, which is part of why it is used for heavy-metal removal, so I don't put it into a metal thing or use a metal spoon. I use glass for ozonating and storing it whenever I can.
a2-b154: The ZHoly3O ferment contains more than just fermented beet juice, but you can ferment your own beet juice or even use other ferments. I found fermented beet made with apple vinegar and salt was best so far, though kimchi and kombucha also helped. Most yogurts weren't fermented enough to work, and apple vinegar by itself only helped a little. Smelling the ferment helps a lot. Drinking a spoonful can also help, although it may cause itching in somebody who breaks down histamine poorly, which then requires activated charcoal to reduce gut histamine.
a1-charcoal:
Activated charcoal helps with toxins in the gut, but drugs bind to it too, so it can flatten or reduce a trip, and that's why I don't treat charcoal and zeolite as interchangeable.

That makes charcoal the one to give when the goal is to stop more of the drug being absorbed, or when the gut itself is toxic. I use zeolite instead when I want to keep the trip and only make the gut feel better.

Medicines bind to charcoal too, so I'd think twice before giving it to someone who depends on a medicine, and if medics come, I'd tell them charcoal was taken.
